items.text: Pfff, kur te. Postal si izseljeni, zdaj se ti za nas ne mudi. Ti s tujci zazrt samozaničevalec.
items.q: An old friend teases Amir for moving abroad, calling him a foreigner-worshiping sellout. Does this sound like real teasing slang?
before: – Oprosti mi, pri Bogu.

items.text: Leva stran je nevarna. Tista rdeča vrata so hiša enega zelo jeznega starca. Še bolj jezen kot Baba.
items.q: A boy warns his little brothers about a scary neighbor. Does it sound like a child talking?
before: Potem je vedno pokazal tisto hišo z velikimi rdečimi vrati. Govoril je:

items.text: Na drugi strani šole je pokopališče. Zelo staro je. Nekaterim grobovom manjkajo kamni. Vidijo se kosti mrtvih.
items.q: A boy tries to scare his little brothers about an old graveyard. Does it sound like a child?
before: Letos grem tja tudi jaz. Če me učitelj udari z ravnilom, bom povedal Maman. Ghassem je vedno rekel:

items.text: Dobro, daj malo. Ampak ne premalo. Malo, samo malo manj.
items.q: A four-year-old bargains with his mother over salt on his green plums. Does it sound like a small child?
before: Rekel sem:

items.text: Tretja faza je ena ulica. Ulica je res dolga.
items.q: A boy explains a big word with a child's logic. Does it sound like a child talking?
before: Po poti je rekel:

items.q: Maman, a little hard of hearing, catches only the end of the film title 'Solze in nasmehi'. Does her question come across?
before: – Otroci, naj prenesem film Solze in nasmehi, da ga gledamo nocoj?
Maman obrne glavo in reče:

items.text: Najprej pridite in dokumentirajte ta palec, potem pa snemajte film o čemerkoli hočete.
items.q: Hooman sticks up his thumb, a rude gesture in Iran, to mock Farid's film idea. Does this read as a rude joke?
before: – Fantje, dajmo posneti dokumentarni film o naši sobi.
Hooman je izvlekel roko izpod odeje in rekel:

items.text: Dvaintrideset mesecev je, kar vas ljubim. Od daleč. Ne da bi vedeli.
items.q: He finally declares his love to a girl he has always addressed politely. Does the polite 'vas' feel right here?
before: Šel sem in se ustavil pod platano na drugi strani pločnika ulice Valiasr ter čakal, da se Niloofar loči od drugih, da bi stopil naprej in ji iz obraza v obraz povedal, da jo ljubim.

items.text: Je Arasteh prirejena oblika od araasteh, urejenega?
items.q: The guard puns: Arasteh is Persian araasteh (neat), one letter trimmed. Would Slovenian readers get it? If not, what word could carry it?
before: – Gospod Arasteh.
Obrnem glavo k njemu.

items.text: Pir tu pir? Torej od starešine do starešine?
items.q: Amir mishears the computer term 'pir tu pir' as 'Stari tu Stari', his own nickname. Would Slovenian readers get it? If not, what word could?
before: – Kaj je zdaj to?
– Neke vrste elektronski denar, pir tu pir.
Rekel sem:

items.text: Dal bi vse zate, Nini-jan. Tvoja glava tako dobro dela.
items.q: Amir fondly praises his mother, whom the family lovingly call Nini, for her quick wit. Does this sound warm and natural?
before: Rečem:

items.text: Ženske? Rada bi. Kdor ga hoče, ga vzame zase. Damo še nekaj zraven.
items.q: Maman says she wishes he had chased women: any woman can have him, with something extra thrown in. Does this read clearly?
before: – Mislim, da ni tekal za drugimi ženskami.

items.text: Ne. Dokler je ta nit v tvoji roki, se ne boš izgubil. Drugi konec je v moji roki.
items.q: Maman reassures her small son, who is afraid of getting lost. Does this sound like a mother talking to a child?
before: Maman je vedno rekla:

items.text: Kakor tisto: bolj ko razmišljaš o teh desetih besedah, hujša je usra-, to, vrtoglavica.
items.q: The stammering speaker nearly repeats the crude phrase, stops, and says a polite word instead. Does that come through?
before: – To je. To poslušaj. Ti, za božjo voljo, poslušaj. »Tisto vino, ki je tam, je resnica ne prispodoba.« Tudi to je isto. Kakor tista slika, ki jo je kazala tvoja pr-pr-prijateljica.

items.text: Potakni nos v vsak košček. Stari so vedno govorili: pokukaj v vsak zadnji kotiček.
items.q: Maman urges her son to explore and quotes an old saying. Does it sound like a folk saying she would use?
before: – Mm-hm, prav delaš. Dokler imaš priložnost, pojdi in si oglej vse vasi.
